source: Typical practical rates per technology (rules of thumb, units per hour). Edit here, never in code.

SKEW.label: Angled roller merge
SKEW.note: Side line joins at 30-45 deg over slightly skewed rollers: no lift, no cycle stop, fewer drives, product keeps moving. Items leave rotated or off-centre: align right after (side guides, skewed rollers, centring)

POPUP.label: Pop-up wheel transfer
POPUP.note: Rows of small powered wheels between the rollers pop up and steer the load out (90 deg transfer, or 15-75 deg divert/merge). 25-40 cycles/min: ~1,500-2,400/h, usually the bottleneck

STRIP.label: High-performance divert (HPD)
STRIP.note: Cassettes of small swivelling rollers (or strip belts / pivoting wheels) in the main bed steer units out of the moving mainline at 30-45 deg (reversed: dynamic merge). Lives and dies with gap control; keep both lanes clear downstream

ARB.label: Angled-roller belt
ARB.note: Angled rollers in the belt, activated from below: divert / merge at full line speed, contactless. Very expensive; controls know-how; belt modules are wear items

PUSHER.label: Pusher divert
PUSHER.note: Pushes the unit off the line at 90 deg into a reject lane or rarely used exit. Cheap and compact, but loud and hard on the load: sturdy items only, needs a clear gap

BELT.label: Pop-up belt transfer (RAT)
BELT.note: Belt strips rise between the rollers, lift the unit and carry it off at 90 deg without turning it: the workhorse for totes and cartons. 25-40 cycles/min (~1,500-2,400/h): almost always the bottleneck, size it before the straight runs. The divert lane must be as wide as the unit is long

CHAIN.label: Pop-up chain transfer
CHAIN.note: Two or three chain strands between the rollers lift the load and move it sideways: heavy loads and pallets, slow

ARB.label: Angled-roller element
ARB.note: Centre / align or turn 90 deg in motion, contactless

PIVOT.label: Fixed-pivot turn
PIVOT.note: A pin at the line edge turns a rigid load 90 deg in motion; each pivot suits a limited size window

SPIRAL.label: Spiral conveyor
SPIRAL.note: Continuous vertical transport at high rate on a small footprint; one in, one out; 0.5-1.0 m/s

LIFT.label: S- / C-conveyor (continuous vertical)
LIFT.note: Continuous vertical conveyor, one item per platform, ~2 x 2 m footprint; S: out on the opposite side (through a mezzanine), C: in and out on the same side. 1,000-1,400/h

RAT.label: 90 deg pop-up belt transfer
RAT.note: Belt strips lift the unit and carry it off at 90 deg; 25-40 cycles/min, usually the bottleneck

BUFFER.label: ZPA accumulation
BUFFER.note: Zero-pressure accumulation: one motor roller and one photo-eye per zone

CURVE.label: Powered roller curve
CURVE.note: Tapered rollers, inner radius 600-800 mm; a belt curve above ~1.5 m/s or for exact orientation

WRAPPER.label: Pallet wrapper
WRAPPER.note: Conveyorised turntable stretch wrapper: 40-45 loads/h (Handle It FA-4000, Lantech Q Automatic), up to 16 rpm, wrap height 2.2-2.3 m
